violated_contract: Offline-sync pending audio is refused permanently by the server once it ages past the automatic-recovery window (SYNC_BACKFILL_MAX_AGE_SECONDS, 30 days; the 422 backfill_lookback_exceeded response retires the recording terminal). A drain that always attempts the newest pending WALs first spends every interrupted run — rate-limit break, cancelled sync, app backgrounding — on the audio with the most deadline slack, so the oldest recordings are attempted last indefinitely, age past the window, and are refused without any per-file failure ever being observed: newer audio syncs normally while oldest_pending_age grows for weeks.
canonical_prevention: Order the drain by deadline, not recency: live capture (the only audio still able to claim its running conversation) leads newest-first, and everything older drains oldest-first, so any truncation costs the audio with the most slack instead of the least. Pin it with batch-selection tests that feed mixed live/historical WAL sets and assert the oldest historical WAL forms the first batch while live capture still leads and conversation grouping is unchanged.
